In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RRNS codes constitute a novel family of maximum-minimum distance binary block codes, exhibiting the same distance properties with Reed-Solomon (RS) codes.
RRNS codes exhibit a performance that is comparable to that of Reed-Solomon and BCH codes.
RRNS codes can provide the best performance among the class of maximum-minimum distance linear block codes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have introduced a novel class of RRNS codes, and we have proposed systematic RRNS codes, as well as binary to RRNS symbol mapping techniques.

the proposed systematic RRNS codes can achieve the performance of the best binary block codes, while their encoding and decoding complexity is lower than the corresponding complexity of the best binary linear block codes, and the decoding complexity of the proposed systematic RR NS codes is comparable to that of the best nonbinary block codes.
we have introduced a novel family of maximum-minimum distance codes, namely the redundant residue number system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Chase algorithm can be used for soft decoding of RRNS and BCH codes, and the soft-input/ soft-output Chase algorithm can be utilized to provide iterative decoding for RRNS codes.
RRNS codes are very attractive for the design of efficient turbo codes, as they exhibit a high degree of parallelism, which allows for a low-complexity iterative soft decoding.
systematic RRNS codes exhibit a better upper-bound performance than nonsystematic RRNs codes, when ML soft decoding is employed.
